hero.headline: Florida attorney general investigates solar companies as Treasure Coast complaints mount
hero.teaser: Seniors vs. Crime, a division of the Florida attorney general's office, opened investigations into solar panel companies after Treasure Coast homeowners reported broken systems, damaged roofs and inability to sell homes due to costly 25-year loans.
hero.body:
A wave of complaints from Treasure Coast homeowners has prompted the Florida attorney general's office to launch formal investigations into solar panel companies. At least six families have come forward with similar stories about aggressive door-to-door sales tactics that promised significant savings on electricity bills. The investigation uncovered court records and lawsuits showing a troubling pattern of elderly homeowners who say they were misled during the sales process. Seniors vs. Crime, a division of the attorney general's office, became involved after watching WPTV's initial investigation into the issue.

The financial impact on affected homeowners has been severe. Mike Schopp is locked into a 25-year, $60,000 loan and now pays nearly double his previous electricity costs. Jane Bibee's $40,000 solar loan has made it nearly impossible to sell her home. Paula Wass and David McCauley are still paying off $39,000 for panels that never reduced their nearly $300-monthly FPL bills. The couple discovered their system stopped working in November 2024, and an engineering report found moisture intrusion at the solar panel brackets, with unclear approval status for the installation brackets. Wass noted the problems were particularly frustrating because the installation occurred on a brand new home.

Data obtained by WPTV shows nearly 750 consumer complaints have been filed in Florida against three solar companies examined in the investigation. The attorney general has opened formal investigations into two of those companies, with active litigation filed against the third. Marty Jacobsen, deputy director with Seniors vs. Crime, explained that his office receives many complaints about fraudulent solar deals. "Oftentimes, these rogue products are obsolete. They'll go on your roof, they can't connect to the grid, but there's a 25-year warranty with a company that doesn't exist anymore, so you can't get service," Jacobsen said. The pattern of failed installations and defunct companies has spawned at least two class-action lawsuits against multiple solar companies.

Resources are available for affected homeowners. Seniors vs. Crime has helped multiple homeowners cancel contracts and recover money through mediation and negotiation at no cost. Some homeowners may be eligible for Florida's Construction Recovery Fund, a state fund financed by permit fees that compensates consumers for contractor misconduct. Attorneys have successfully recovered money for some homeowners through litigation. The attorney general's office and Seniors vs. Crime encourage anyone experiencing similar problems to file a complaint with the attorney general's office.

cards.headline: Martin County Sheriff increases enforcement after 5 traffic deaths in 4 days
cards.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced increased enforcement on major roadways following five traffic fatalities in four days, including a double fatal cr.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office is increasing enforcement on major roadways following five traffic fatalities in four days. A double fatal crash Monday on Florida's Turnpike near Mile Marker 132 outside Palm City exemplified the recent deadly stretch. A Tesla traveling southbound contacted another vehicle, veered through an opening in the median into the northbound lane and struck a semi-truck. Two people were killed and one was injured and taken to the hospital. The crash shut down northbound and southbound lanes for hours while the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol investigated.

Richard Cassoon, who works at Stryker Electric just off the Turnpike, witnessed the impact. "It was like a loud boom," Cassoon said. "You could see all the trucks, everything, everybody swerving. It was like everybody just like trying to come to like a complete halt." Captain Joseph Collazo with the Martin County Sheriff's Office said the recent crashes are top of mind for deputies. With Fourth of July travel ramping up this week, Collazo said the department will increase enforcement on major corridors throughout Martin County, including U.S. Highway 1. Collazo urged drivers to slow down during the holiday week. "We just ask everyone to slow down and be patient," Collazo said. "We're all trying to get to somewhere, and it's not worth losing our lives over."

cards.headline: Property tax amendment threatens $8 billion revenue cut to Florida local governments
cards.teaser: A constitutional amendment pushed by Governor Ron DeSantis onto the November ballot could reduce local government revenues by more than $8 billion in fiscal year 2027-28 and more than $14 billion the following year, according to House staff estimates.
cards.body:
The property tax amendment on Florida's November ballot could reduce local government revenues by more than $8 billion in Fiscal Year 2027-28 and more than $14 billion the following year, according to House staff estimates. Miami-Dade County faces a projected $445 million revenue hit by Fiscal Year 2028-29, while Broward County faces a $326 million loss. Local governments will still need to fund fire rescue, police, drainage, roads, parks, libraries, emergency response and basic infrastructure. These costs will likely be covered through fire fees, stormwater fees, garbage assessments, utility taxes, parking fees, permit fees, special assessments, local sales tax increases, delayed maintenance and reduced services.

A coalition of organized labor, local governments, first responders, housing advocates, the Florida Education Association and the Florida Chamber of Commerce has opposed the amendment. The Chamber warned the Governor in writing that without firm guardrails, the amendment would shift the tax burden onto local businesses and renters. A formal opposition campaign called Stop Unfair Tax Shifts, chaired by former Leon County Commissioner Bryan Desloge, has launched. In 2024, North Dakota voters rejected a nearly identical property tax elimination proposal by a two-to-one margin, opposing it in all 53 counties. A lawsuit filed in Leon County Circuit Court argues the ballot summary promotes rather than explains the amendment, using campaign language like "ensuring funding for core services" and "protecting small businesses."

cards.headline: Fort Pierce and Port St. Lucie celebrate America's 250th birthday with fireworks and festivities Saturday
cards.teaser: America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone.
cards.body:
America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone. From sunrise 5Ks and golf cart parades to drone shows, time capsule openings and spectacular fireworks displays, there is something for everyone this Independence Day.

Fort Pierce and Port St. Lucie are among numerous municipalities hosting celebrations. Delray Beach's annual Fourth of July Celebration begins at 8 a.m. and draws more than 20,000 people to East Atlantic Avenue and A1A. The day includes a 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament at the south end of the municipal beach from 8 a.m. to noon and a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs. At 5 p.m., the main festivities begin with the opening of a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule at the Main Stage at A1A, followed by a 60-foot flag raising with the National Anthem at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue at 6 p.m. Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns with events including the Firecracker 5K at 7:15 a.m. at Florida Atlantic University and the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament at 8 a.m. A Fabulous Fourth Block Party runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Sugar Sand Park, with the Fabulous Finale at Countess de Hoernle Park from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m., featuring a 20-minute fireworks display at 9:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Delray Beach to open 50-year-old time capsule during Fourth of July celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will open a historic time capsule during its Fourth of July celebration on Saturday.
cards.body:
Delray Beach will open a historic time capsule during its Fourth of July celebration on Saturday at Atlantic Avenue and A1A. The capsule was sealed and buried in 1976 when America celebrated its 200th birthday. The ceremony begins at 5 p.m. as part of the city's Fourth of July festivities.

David E. Randolph, a former city council member who was in office when the capsule was sealed, contributed a collection of his written thoughts about his race, education, and highlights and awards. After the ceremony, items from the time capsule, including Randolph's written thoughts, will go on display at the Delray Beach Historical Society. The annual Fourth of July celebration draws more than 20,000 people and features food trucks, vendors, children's activities, live music, and a fireworks show at 9 p.m.

cards.headline: Vero Beach nonprofit needs box truck to deliver 100-plus boxes for Venezuela earthquake relief
cards.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies for Venezuela earthquake relief. The organization is urgently calling on the community to donate the use of a box truck to transport the supplies to Miami.
cards.body:
A Vero Beach nonprofit organization has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies for Venezuela earthquake relief and is now calling on the community for urgent assistance. Latinas Nexus Network is working with Global Empowerment Mission in Miami to deliver crucial supplies to Venezuela, which is recovering from a 7.5-magnitude earthquake. The boxes are packed with everything from diapers to medical supplies. "We have been doing this since Friday afternoon," said Lourana Navarro, founder of Latinas Nexus Network. The response from the community exceeded expectations, according to Juliana Marino, co-founder of the organization.

However, the volume of donations is more than the organization can transport on its own. "We thought we were just going to put everything in our cars and we were going to drive to Miami. And there's no more room," Marino said. The organization is urgently requesting the community donate the use of a 12 to 16-foot box truck to move the supplies south. Organizers need the truck no later than Thursday to load supplies for delivery to Global Empowerment Mission in Miami on Friday. The cause is personal for Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and has family near the earthquake's epicenter. Anyone who can help is asked to contact Navarro at (954) 205-0700 or Marino at (772) 913-0805.

cards.headline: Boca Raton hosts Fabulous Fourth 2026 with Firecracker 5K and fireworks at Countess de Hoernle Park
cards.teaser: Boca Raton celebrates America's 250th birthday Saturday with a full day of events including a 7:15 a.m. Firecracker 5K at Florida Atlantic University and a 20-minute fireworks display.
cards.body:
Boca Raton continues its 68-year Independence Day tradition with Fabulous Fourth 2026 on Saturday, July 4, featuring events throughout the city. The Firecracker 5K begins at 7:15 a.m. at Florida Atlantic University, 777 Glades Road, with $40 registration and no on-site registration available. At 8 a.m., the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament starts at Patch Reef Park for pickleball and The Racquet Center for tennis, with fees ranging from $35 to $50. The Fabulous Fourth Block Party runs from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Sugar Sand Park, 300 S. Military Trail, offering free admission with kids' crafts, yard games, a DJ and food trucks.

The Fabulous Finale takes place from 6:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park, 1000 Spanish River Blvd., featuring live music at 6:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. A 20-minute fireworks display begins at 9:10 p.m. Free parking is available at Boca Raton Innovation Campus (BRiC) with entry from Yamato Road, and free trolley service runs from 6:30 p.m. through the end of the event, with strollers required to be fully collapsed to board. No pets, coolers, sparklers, drones, alcohol or glass bottles are permitted. A1A will be closed at the Deerfield/Boca border from 7 p.m. until Deerfield Beach fireworks conclude.

hero.headline: Lake Worth Beach to feature first-ever drone show for Fourth of July
hero.teaser: Lake Worth Beach will celebrate America's 250th birthday with its first-ever drone show, featuring 300 drones in a 15-minute display at Bryant Park.
hero.body:
Lake Worth Beach will celebrate America's 250th anniversary with its inaugural drone light show during the city's Fourth of July festivities at Bryant Park. The event, expected to draw approximately 10,000 people, will feature 300 drones performing a 15-minute aerial display at 8:45 p.m. Spectators will have the best view of the drone show from Bryant Park while facing southwest. The celebration is free to attend and offers a full day of entertainment for families and visitors.

The evening's entertainment lineup begins at 7 p.m. with a concert by Sekond Nature, followed by a skydiving performance at 7:45 p.m. The All Veteran Group will execute the skydiving performance, which includes a tandem jump by Vice Mayor Mimi May carrying a special American flag commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary. After the skydivers land, Elton and the Jets, an Elton John tribute band, will take the stage for concerts at 8:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m. A traditional fireworks display will conclude the evening at 9 p.m., featuring six minutes of pyrotechnics with more than 11,700 shots.

Earlier activities throughout the day provide additional entertainment options. The Neighborhood Association Presidents' Council will host the Great American Raft Race at noon, offering water-based competition and fun. At 5:30 p.m., the city will hold a hot dog eating contest with six contestants competing for recognition.

Attendees should plan ahead for parking and transportation. The city recommends using ride-share services, with drop-off locations available at Fourth Avenue South and South Lakeside Drive at South Bryant Park. The Lake Worth Beach Bridge will be closed to both vehicles and pedestrians from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. to accommodate the anticipated crowd and ensure public safety during the peak entertainment hours. Those planning to attend should arrive early to secure viewing spots, particularly for the drone show, which offers a unique spectacle not yet seen in the area's previous Independence Day celebrations.

cards.headline: Boca Raton businesses collect supplies for Venezuela earthquake victims
cards.teaser: Local businesses in Boca Raton are continuing efforts to support families affected by the devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela last week, leaving thousands dead and even more missing.
cards.body:
GalaFresh Supermarket West Boca Raton and Doctor Chicha restaurant are collecting supplies and monetary donations for families affected by earthquakes that struck Venezuela last week. Franky Jorge, owner of GalaFresh Supermarket West Boca Raton, said he moved quickly after hearing about the earthquakes. Jorge noted that many of his customers and friends are from Venezuela, and as a Latino business owner, the disaster felt personal. The donations will be taken to Global Empowerment Mission in Doral and then shipped to families in Venezuela.

Pamela Rodriguez, owner of Doctor Chicha, said dozens of volunteers sorted through non-perishable foods, baby supplies, clothes and more. Rodriguez described the community's response as overwhelming, saying the facility was completely full. One volunteer was an earthquake survivor herself who told Rodriguez she spent four days trapped under rubble before being rescued. Both business owners emphasized the importance of continued support. Rodriguez said the most important thing is to keep donating, while Jorge urged the community not to forget Venezuela and to assist wherever disaster strikes.

cards.headline: Greenacres to host Independence Day celebration at Samuel J. Ferreri Community Park
cards.teaser: The City of Greenacres will host its annual Independence Day Celebration from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m. at Samuel J. Ferreri Community Park.
cards.body:
The free event features live music entertainment, arts and crafts, food and craft vendors, a stilt walker, contests, games, prizes and a fireworks display. Cash and credit cards will be accepted, with small bills preferred. The city noted there are no refunds available.

Personal fireworks or sparklers are not allowed at the celebration. The event is described as patriotic and family-friendly. Samuel J. Ferreri Community Park will host all activities throughout the evening.

cards.headline: Delray Beach to host snorkeling tours of S.S. Inchulva shipwreck on July Fourth
cards.teaser: Snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva 'Delray Wreck' will be offered from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturday as part of Fourth of July activities.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration will feature snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva shipwreck from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The tours will run alongside other daytime activities at the municipal beach, including the 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament from 8 a.m. to noon at the south end of the beach and a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs, also running from 8 a.m. to noon.

The city's annual Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition for over 50 years, draws more than 20,000 people. All-day activities include food trucks, vendors, arts and crafts, face painting, glitter tattoos, carnival games, a photo booth, and toddler soft play. The main evening festivities begin at 5 p.m. at East Atlantic Avenue and A1A. Visitors are urged to park west of the Intracoastal Bridge, where parking lots are available throughout the city. Free rides are available through the FreeBee app in the downtown area, and Tri-Rail runs a holiday schedule. For more information, call (561) 243-7250, option 3.

cards.headline: Delray Beach to raise 60-foot flag with National Anthem during Fourth of July celebration
cards.teaser: A 60-foot flag raising with the National Anthem will take place at 6 p.m. at the corner of Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue in Delray Beach.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's annual Fourth of July Celebration will take place Saturday, July 4, 2026, at East Atlantic Avenue and A1A, drawing more than 20,000 people to the family-friendly tradition that has run for over 50 years. The event begins with daytime activities at 8 a.m., including a 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament at the south end of municipal beach from 8 a.m. to noon, a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs, and snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva "Delray Wreck" from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

All-day activities include food trucks, vendors, arts and crafts, face painting, glitter tattoos, carnival games, a photo booth, and toddler soft play. Fireworks will conclude the celebration. For more information, call (561) 243-7250, option 3.

hero.headline: Vacant Nordstrom at Mall at Wellington Green could become 620-unit apartment complex
hero.teaser: Bainbridge Companies submitted plans to convert 18 acres of the empty Nordstrom store into a 620-unit multifamily apartment complex in Wellington. The existing building would be demolished if the project is approved.
hero.body:
Bainbridge Companies has submitted plans to transform the vacant Nordstrom at the Mall at Wellington Green into a 620-unit multifamily apartment complex on 18 acres. The existing building would be demolished if the project is approved. Village Manager Jim Barnes said the development would include one-, two-, and three-bedroom units with shared amenities, three towers, and a parking structure. He noted the project addresses a broader housing shortage not only in the county but throughout the state and beyond.

Some residents oppose the proposal. Richard Meyers, who has lived in Wellington for more than a decade, said he opposes adding more apartments to the area, citing existing apartment complexes around the mall. Gaby Martinez raised concerns about traffic, saying added density could create bottlenecks on local roads. Barnes countered that new development could benefit remaining retailers, noting that Macy's, Dillard's, and JCPenney continue to perform well. He said the Macy's at the Mall at Wellington Green is the highest-performing store in the state. No timeline or cost estimate has been announced, and the plans have not been approved.

cards.teaser: The city of Lake Worth Beach is celebrating America's 250th birthday with its first-ever drone show on Saturday at Bryant Park. The event also includes live music, a skydiving performance, and fireworks.
cards.body:
Lake Worth Beach is celebrating America's 250th birthday on Saturday, July 4, 2026, at Bryant Park with its first-ever drone show, live music and a skydiving performance. The event is free and expected to draw 10,000 people. The celebration begins at noon with the Great American Raft Race, hosted by the Neighborhood Association Presidents' Council. At 5:30 p.m., a hot dog eating contest featuring 6 contestants will take place, with details on how to apply coming soon via city social media.

Entertainment continues throughout the evening with a concert by Sekond Nature at 7 p.m. followed by a skydiving performance by the All Veteran Group at 7:45 p.m., including a tandem jump by Vice Mayor Mimi May carrying a special American flag commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary. The drone light show featuring 300 drones runs for 15 minutes at 8:45 p.m., best viewed from Bryant Park facing southwest. Concerts by Elton and the Jets, an Elton John tribute band, are scheduled for 8:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m., with a fireworks display featuring 6 minutes and 11,700-plus shots at 9 p.m. The Lake Worth Beach Bridge will be closed to vehicles and pedestrians from 8 to 10 p.m. Ride-share drop-off is available at Fourth Avenue South and South Lakeside Drive at South Bryant Park.

cards.headline: Boca Raton to host full day of Independence Day events including 20-minute fireworks display
cards.teaser: Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns with a full day of events celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The evening Fabulous Finale at Countess de Hoernle Park features waterfront live music and a 20-minute fireworks spectacular.
cards.body:
Boca Raton will celebrate America's 250th anniversary on Saturday, July 4, 2026, with its Fabulous Fourth 2026, a full day of events across multiple city locations. The celebration begins at 7:15 a.m. with the Firecracker 5K at Florida Atlantic University, 777 Glades Road, requiring $40 registration with no on-site registration available. At 8 a.m., the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament starts, with pickleball at Patch Reef Park and tennis at The Racquet Center, costing $35 to $50 for pickleball and $35 to $43.75 for tennis. From 1 to 4 p.m., the Fabulous Fourth Block Party at Sugar Sand Park, 300 S. Military Trail, offers free kids' crafts, yard games, a DJ, and food trucks.

The Fabulous Finale runs from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park, 1000 Spanish River Boulevard, featuring free admission, live music at 6:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m., and a 20-minute fireworks display at 9:10 p.m. Food trucks and vendors will operate on-site. Blankets and lawn chairs are welcome, but pets, coolers, sparklers, drones, alcohol, and glass bottles are prohibited. Free filtered water is available. Free parking is offered at Boca Raton Innovation Campus with entrance from Yamato Road, while ride-share drop-off is at 4530 Technology Way. Free trolley service runs from 6:30 p.m. through the event's end, though strollers must be fully collapsed to board. A1A will close at the Deerfield/Boca border from 7 p.m. until Deerfield Beach fireworks conclude.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County planners recommend approval of controversial AI data center near Loxahatchee
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County planning staff have recommended that county commissioners approve Project Tango AI data center, despite months of pushback from residents in the western communities. The proposed site sits approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and Saddleview Elementary School.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County planning staff have recommended that county commissioners approve the controversial Project Tango AI data center, despite months of pushback from residents in the western communities. The recommendation does not reflect an opinion on the project, according to Palm Beach County Mayor and Commissioner Sara Baxter, who represents the area where the center would be built. Baxter said the staff recommendation simply means the project has met certain legal criteria required by the county. The proposed data center site sits approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddleview Elementary School.

County staff are requiring the applicant to make several changes to reduce potential impacts on nearby residents, including limiting potable water use, implementing deeper safeguards for lithium iron batteries, providing updated sound studies from the Loxahatchee National Wildlife Refuge, and limiting daily water use to 100,000 gallons per day. Despite these conditions, residents say the changes are insufficient. Baxter, who has publicly opposed the project and will recuse herself from the vote, plans to push commissioners to approve a moratorium on future data centers. She confirmed that if approved, Project Tango would not fall under the moratorium. A planning and zoning meeting is scheduled for Thursday, July 2, expected to draw hundreds of protesters. A new law dealing with large-scale data centers takes effect Wednesday, July 1.

hero.headline: Vero Beach nonprofit needs box truck to deliver 100+ boxes for Venezuela earthquake relief
hero.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies for Venezuela earthquake relief and urgently needs a box truck to transport them to Miami.
hero.body:
Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach has collected more than 100 boxes of supplies to help Venezuela recover from a devastating 7.5-magnitude earthquake. The organization is partnering with Global Empowerment Mission in Miami to transport and deliver the donations, but they need community assistance to complete their mission. Leaders say they must secure a box truck by Thursday to load the supplies and transport them to Miami on Friday.

Founder Lourana Navarro and co-founder Juliana Marino launched their collection effort Friday afternoon and were amazed by the community's response. The boxes contain essential items including diapers and medical supplies needed by people affected by the earthquake. "The community has come together. They all came forward and brought something," Marino said. The overwhelming generosity created an unexpected problem: the organization ran out of space to transport everything using personal vehicles alone.

What began as a plan to move donations in their own cars quickly became impossible as boxes continued arriving from the community. "We thought we were just going to put everything in our cars and we were going to drive to Miami. And there's no more room," Marino explained. The organization is now making an urgent appeal for someone to donate the use of a 12 to 16-foot box truck to transport all the collected supplies. For Navarro, the cause holds deep personal significance. She was born in Venezuela and has family living near the earthquake's epicenter. "It really kills me to see thousands, hundreds of thousands of people in the streets," she said, emphasizing why this relief effort matters so much to her.

Navarro and Marino say they cannot complete this relief mission without the community's continued support. "We put it together, now we need to deliver," Marino said. Anyone with access to an appropriate box truck or who wants to help in other ways is encouraged to contact Navarro at 954-205-0700 or Marino at 772-913-0805. The tight timeline means organizers need commitments quickly, as they plan to load the truck Thursday and transport the supplies to Global Empowerment Mission in Miami the following day.

cards.headline: Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties score high in Florida school grades released
cards.teaser: Florida released school grades for the 2025-26 academic year, with Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties scoring high marks.
cards.body:
Florida released school grades for the 2025-26 academic year. Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties all scored high in the statewide assessment.

The three Treasure Coast counties received favorable marks in the state grading system. The results reflect performance during the school year that just concluded.

The Florida school grading system evaluates districts and individual schools on academic performance. The high scores for the three counties indicate strong educational outcomes across the Treasure Coast region.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast communities to vote on best girls athlete during 2025-26 season
cards.teaser: Treasure Coast residents can vote for the best girls athlete during the 2025-26 season.
cards.body:
Treasure Coast residents can vote for the best girls athlete during the 2025-26 season. The voting is now open for residents across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

The voting allows the community to recognize the top female athletic performers from the school year that just concluded. Athletes from high schools across the three-county region are eligible for the recognition.

The voting period is currently underway for Treasure Coast area residents. Community members can participate in selecting the top girls athlete from the season.

The recognition highlights athletic achievements at local high schools during the 2025-26 academic year. The winner will be determined by community voting across the Treasure Coast region.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial time capsule Saturday during Fourth of July celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will open its 1976 Bicentennial time capsule on Saturday during the city's annual Fourth of July celebration, which draws more than 20,000 people.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's annual Fourth of July Celebration will mark America's 250th birthday on Saturday with the opening of a 1976 Bicentennial time capsule at the Main Stage at A1A. The city's family-friendly tradition, which has been held for over 50 years, draws more than 20,000 people. A 60-foot flag raising with the National Anthem will take place at 6 p.m. at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue, followed by live music and entertainment by Digital Vibez and fireworks.

Daytime activities begin at 8 a.m., including the 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament at the south end of the municipal beach and a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs running from 8 a.m. to noon. Snorkeling and scuba dive tours of the S.S. Inchulva "Delray Wreck" are available from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Throughout the day, food trucks, vendors, arts and crafts, face painting, glitter tattoos, carnival games, photo booths, and toddler soft play will be available. The public is urged to park west of the Intracoastal Bridge, with free rides available through the FreeBee app. For more information, call 561-243-7250, option 3.

cards.headline: Jupiter family spends over $1,000 fixing passport errors before England trip
cards.teaser: A Jupiter family paid more than $1,000 to correct passport errors after receiving documents with multiple mistakes through the expedited U.S. State Department system.
cards.body:
Dr. Thomas McCain of Jupiter contacted WPTV after his family received passports with multiple errors and spent more than $1,000 to correct them before an international trip to England. McCain's passport contained one error, while his three children each had the same clerical error. His middle son's middle name was also incorrect, bringing the total to five errors across the family's passports. The errors were discovered a month ago and led to hours of phone calls, multiple trips to the Palm Beach Gardens post office, and ultimately a trip to Miami for corrections.

McCain said his heart goes out to people who are not in a financial position to deal with such problems or unable to take off from work. The State Department confirmed it has been going through large layoffs and reorganization. A State Department spokesperson said the department strives to issue every passport accurately and has quality assurance measures in place. If a department error is identified, the State Department will correct it at no charge. Passports typically cost about $60, and waiting for a new one without paying to expedite can take as long as two months.

cards.headline: Boca Raton hosts Fabulous Fourth 2026 with Firecracker 5K and fireworks at Countess de Hoernle Park
cards.teaser: Boca Raton celebrates America's 250th birthday Saturday with a full day of events including a 7:15 a.m. Firecracker 5K at Florida Atlantic University and a 20-minute fireworks display.
cards.body:
Boca Raton continues its 68-year Independence Day tradition with Fabulous Fourth 2026 on Saturday, July 4, featuring events throughout the city. The Firecracker 5K begins at 7:15 a.m. at Florida Atlantic University, 777 Glades Road, with $40 registration and no on-site registration available. At 8 a.m., the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament starts at Patch Reef Park for pickleball and The Racquet Center for tennis, with fees ranging from $35 to $50. The Fabulous Fourth Block Party runs from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Sugar Sand Park, 300 S. Military Trail, offering free admission with kids' crafts, yard games, a DJ and food trucks.

The Fabulous Finale takes place from 6:30 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park, 1000 Spanish River Blvd., featuring live music at 6:30 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. A 20-minute fireworks display begins at 9:10 p.m. Free parking is available at Boca Raton Innovation Campus (BRiC) with entry from Yamato Road, and free trolley service runs from 6:30 p.m. through the end of the event, with strollers required to be fully collapsed to board. No pets, coolers, sparklers, drones, alcohol or glass bottles are permitted. A1A will be closed at the Deerfield/Boca border from 7 p.m. until Deerfield Beach fireworks conclude.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach holds first-ever drone light show Saturday with 300 drones at Bryant Park
cards.teaser: Lake Worth Beach celebrates America's 250th birthday Saturday with its first-ever drone light show featuring 300 drones, plus a skydiving performance and fireworks at Bryant Park.
cards.body:
Lake Worth Beach celebrates America's 250th anniversary Saturday with its first-ever drone light show at Bryant Park. The 15-minute show features 300 drones beginning at 8:45 p.m., best viewed from Bryant Park facing southwest. A six-minute fireworks display with more than 11,700 shots follows at 9 p.m. The event is free and expected to draw 10,000 people.

The celebration includes the Great American Raft Race hosted by the Neighborhood Association Presidents' Council at noon, and a hot dog eating contest with six contestants at 5:30 p.m. Sekond Nature performs at 7 p.m., followed by a skydiving performance by the All Veteran Group at 7:45 p.m. that includes a tandem jump by Vice Mayor Mimi May carrying a special American flag commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary. Elton and the Jets, an Elton John tribute band, performs at 8:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m. Ride-share drop-off is at Fourth Avenue South and South Lakeside Drive at South Bryant Park. The Lake Worth Beach Bridge will be closed to vehicles and pedestrians from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
North Palm Beach is hosting a full day of Independence Day festivities on July 4 at the North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse. The free community event brings together residents and visitors for family-friendly activities, live entertainment and a fireworks display at 9 p.m. According to organizers, this year's celebration carries special significance as it also marks America's 250th anniversary, adding extra meaning to the traditional holiday gathering in Palm Beach County.

The day begins with a community pool party starting at 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Attendees can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, various games and activities, food and beverages, and a poolside satellite bar. Event organizers note that the pool deck and surrounding lawn areas will create a festive atmosphere throughout the day. This opening allows families to cool off and enjoy entertainment during the earlier hours before the afternoon activities begin.

At 4:30 p.m., the festivities expand with lawn games and activities designed for all ages. Families can participate in cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and other lawn games. The Clubhouse will also open its Fourth of July barbecue buffet at this time, offering food options for guests. Live music from the band Solstice Reign is scheduled to begin around 6 p.m., providing entertainment as the evening progresses.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, highlighted the excellent vantage point available for the fireworks display. According to Shipman, the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks finale. The evening fireworks are scheduled to begin at 9 p.m., providing a spectacular conclusion to the day's celebrations. The combination of activities, food, music and the fireworks display creates a comprehensive Independence Day experience for the community, making it a notable tradition for Palm Beach County residents and visitors alike.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
cards.teaser: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season this summer.
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment.

The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Florida Board of Governors approves Stuart Bell as University of Florida president in 15-1 vote
hero.body:
The Florida Board of Governors voted 15-1 Wednesday to approve Stuart Bell as the next president of the University of Florida, concluding a search that has lasted two years. Bell, who previously served as president of the University of Alabama, expressed his commitment to the university during the meeting. "I will serve with integrity. I will serve with humility. I will serve with accountability for this group and to my Board of Trustees," he told the board. He outlined his vision to make UF the best public school in the country, saying "I sense there's a hunger for leadership. There's a hunger for this direction."

Governor Aubrey Edge, who leads First Coast Energy, cast the sole dissenting vote and expressed concerns about Bell's support for diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives. Bell directly addressed these concerns, stating "I want to be very clear and maybe we can set this aside: I'm not coming to Florida to bring DEI or woke back to the state of Florida." Bell holds a background in mechanical engineering and has held several academic leadership positions throughout his career, including serving as provost at Louisiana State University and dean of engineering at the University of Kansas.

The university has been without a permanent president since Ben Sasse resigned in 2024. The board previously attempted to hire University of Michigan President Santa Ono in 2025, but the Board of Governors opposed the decision after elected officials criticized Ono for being too liberal and supporting diversity initiatives. Bell's appointment also faced unexpected resistance from U.S. Senator Rick Scott, who criticized the university for making Bell the sole finalist in what he described as a secretive hiring process. Scott also objected to the decision to overlook interim President Donald Landry, who would receive a 2 million dollar severance package if not selected as permanent president. Board of Governors Chair Alan Levine had raised questions about whether University of Florida Chair Mori Hosseini had exceeded his authority during the hiring process.

Bell's contract will run through June 30, 2031, with an average annual salary of 2.4 million dollars, according to the Gainesville Sun. Hosseini defended the search process at Wednesday's meeting, emphasizing that the board sought more than an administrator. "From the very beginning, our board of trustees and our search committee understood that we were not simply looking for an administrator. We were looking for a leader, someone who could build on this foundation," Hosseini said.

cards.headline: Property tax amendment threatens $8 billion revenue cut to Florida local governments
cards.teaser: A constitutional amendment pushed by Governor Ron DeSantis onto the November ballot could reduce local government revenues by more than $8 billion in fiscal year 2027-28 and more than $14 billion the following year, according to House staff estimates.
cards.body:
The property tax amendment on Florida's November ballot could reduce local government revenues by more than $8 billion in Fiscal Year 2027-28 and more than $14 billion the following year, according to House staff estimates. Miami-Dade County faces a projected $445 million revenue hit by Fiscal Year 2028-29, while Broward County faces a $326 million loss. Local governments will still need to fund fire rescue, police, drainage, roads, parks, libraries, emergency response and basic infrastructure. These costs will likely be covered through fire fees, stormwater fees, garbage assessments, utility taxes, parking fees, permit fees, special assessments, local sales tax increases, delayed maintenance and reduced services.

A coalition of organized labor, local governments, first responders, housing advocates, the Florida Education Association and the Florida Chamber of Commerce has opposed the amendment. The Chamber warned the Governor in writing that without firm guardrails, the amendment would shift the tax burden onto local businesses and renters. A formal opposition campaign called Stop Unfair Tax Shifts, chaired by former Leon County Commissioner Bryan Desloge, has launched. In 2024, North Dakota voters rejected a nearly identical property tax elimination proposal by a two-to-one margin, opposing it in all 53 counties. A lawsuit filed in Leon County Circuit Court argues the ballot summary promotes rather than explains the amendment, using campaign language like "ensuring funding for core services" and "protecting small businesses."

cards.headline: Byron Donalds gains endorsements from Florida's incoming legislative leaders and Attorney General
cards.teaser: U.S. Representative Byron Donalds secured endorsements Wednesday from Senate President-designate Jim Boyd, House Speaker-designate Sam Garrison and Attorney General James Uthmeier in his bid for Florida governor.
cards.body:
Florida's incoming Senate President Kathleen Passidomo and House Speaker Daniel Perez endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds' gubernatorial campaign on Wednesday, followed by Attorney General James Uthmeier's announcement of support. Uthmeier, who was appointed to the office last year and is running to keep it, cited Donalds' policy record and prior state legislative service. "Byron is a Freedom Caucus conservative and proven Florida House leader. He's committed to continuing our fight to punish child predators, support law enforcement, protect the unborn, honor parents' rights, defend the Second Amendment and win against the woke left," Uthmeier said on X.

The endorsements add to support from President Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., House Speaker Mike Johnson, U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ted Cruz, 17 of 19 U.S. House Republicans from Florida, more than 75 percent of Florida House Republicans, nine Florida Senate Republicans, a majority of Florida Sheriffs, Governors Sarah Huckabee Sanders of Arkansas and Jeff Landry of Louisiana, former Florida GOP Chair Christian Ziegler, activist Charlie Kirk and Elon Musk. Donalds has raised more than $81 million through more than 37,000 unique donors, with roughly $65 million in the bank by mid-June. Polling consistently shows Donalds as the clear front-runner to succeed term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis, holding double-digit leads over other GOP contenders including Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, investor James Fishback and former House Speaker Paul Renner.

cards.headline: DeSantis vetoes $3.5 million for air conditioning upgrades at College of the Florida Keys for second year
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis has vetoed $3.5 million for air conditioning infrastructure upgrades at the College of the Florida Keys for the second consecutive year, denying state funding for a project the school says is increasingly urgent as summers grow hotter.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has vetoed $3.5 million for air conditioning infrastructure upgrades at the College of the Florida Keys for the second consecutive year. The appropriation, sought by Doral Republican Sen. Ana Maria Rodriguez and Islamorada Republican Rep. Jim Mooney, would have funded modernization and expansion of the chiller plant system serving the college's Key West campus, including extending chilled-water lines to the campus welding lab, which currently has no air conditioning. The college serves more than 1,500 students, employees and community members, and its Key West campus also houses the Tuga Clinic, a community healthcare facility operated in partnership with the Florida Department of Health.

School officials warned that without upgrades, the aging system risks campus shutdowns during the hottest months, typically May through September, forcing class cancellations at the height of the Keys' summer heat. Rodriguez and Mooney had originally requested $7 million for the full project scope, which includes comprehensive assessment, engineering and construction work across the chiller plant system. The Legislature partially funded the request, appropriating $3.5 million, the same amount DeSantis vetoed from the prior year's budget. DeSantis issued the latest veto Monday after slashing $1.6 billion from the state's 2026-27 budget. The back-to-back cancellations leave the college with no identified alternative funding source, with work expected to run from October 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027.

cards.headline: Consumer confidence in Florida drops to lowest level in two years
cards.teaser: Consumer sentiment in Florida fell for the fourth consecutive month in June, dropping 1.8 points to 71.1 and reaching its lowest level in two years since May 2024, according to a University of Florida survey.
cards.body:
Consumer confidence in Florida continues to decline, according to a University of Florida survey. The consumer sentiment index fell 1.8 points from May to June, dropping from 72.9 to 71.1. Over the past four months, consumer sentiment has fallen 8 points, reaching its lowest level in two years since May 2024, according to Hector H. Sandoval, Director of the Economic Analysis Program at the UF Bureau of Economic and Business Research. Sandoval attributed the pessimism to the reemergence of inflation, which continues to strain household budgets, particularly in everyday categories such as gasoline. Consumers also grew less optimistic when comparing their current finances to a year ago, with that metric dropping 2.1 points from 66.9 in May to 64.8 in June. Floridians' future economic outlook over the next year also weakened, declining from 85.2 in May to 83.9 in June.

Sandoval noted that the economic impact from the war with Iran is providing nagging concerns among consumers. Although gasoline prices have eased from their spring peak as tensions in the Middle East have moderated, some uncertainty surrounding the conflict remains. Florida's unemployment rate was 4.8 percent in May, according to FloridaCommerce, holding steady from April but notably higher than the national figure of 4.3 percent. Sandoval stated that while the national labor market has remained resilient, Florida's labor market has softened, meaning Florida households remain more sensitive to inflation and broader economic uncertainty. The UF survey was conducted between May 1 and June 22 and contacted 394 Floridians across the state by cellphone.

cards.headline: Democrats seek to intervene in Republican Paula Stark's ballot qualification lawsuit
cards.teaser: The Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee and two Democratic candidates are fighting to join Republican Representative Paula Stark's lawsuit to get back on the ballot in House District 47.
cards.body:
The Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee and Democratic candidates Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves are fighting to join Republican Rep. Paula Stark's lawsuit to regain ballot access. Mark Herron, the Florida Democrats' chief election lawyer, said granting relief to Stark will substantially affect the candidacies of the two Democratic candidates who qualified for the House District 47 race and will impact resources the committee will expend in the election.

Stark filed a response this week opposing the Democrats' motion to intervene in her lawsuit against Secretary of State Cord Byrd, Osceola Supervisor of Elections Mary Jane Arrington and Orange County Supervisor of Elections Karen Castor Dentel. Stark argued the two Democrats have "no direct interest" in her qualifying paperwork and that their concern about the committee's resources is speculative and does not establish the direct and immediate interest needed to warrant intervention. The Secretary of State takes no position on the intervention, while lawyers for the two election supervisors did not oppose it. Stark is suing in Leon Circuit Court after failing to qualify for the ballot last month. She said one required form was hand-delivered in Tallahassee but was inadvertently returned to her campaign treasurer and significant other Joel Davis. She argues she should still be allowed to run in House District 47, a traditionally blue district covering St. Cloud, east Kissimmee and a small portion of Orange County.

cards.headline: Tampa Representative Kathy Castor raises $1 million as redistricting forces her into battleground district
cards.teaser: Representative Kathy Castor raised $1 million in the second quarter as a new congressional map shifted her seat from safely Democratic to a district where 55 percent of voters supported Donald Trump in the last presidential election.
cards.body:
Tampa Representative Kathy Castor raised $1 million in the second quarter as redistricting moved her into a battleground district. The support came entirely from outside contributions, including from 7,681 individual donors, with most donations under $100. Castor has now raised more than $2 million as she seeks an 11th term in Congress and closed June with $1.3 million in cash on hand. She previously represented a fairly safe Democratic seat where nearly 53 percent of voters in 2024 supported Democrat Kamala Harris for President and where Castor won 57 percent support in her own reelection bid.

Under new lines crafted by Governor Ron DeSantis' office in a rare mid-decade redistricting, the district shifts eastward into rural southeast Hillsborough County, where about 55 percent of voters supported Republican Donald Trump in the last presidential election. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added Castor to their Frontline program defending incumbents in battleground seats. Eight Republicans qualified to run in Congressional District 14: former state Representative Mike Beltran, construction industry professional Michael Marcel, franchise owner John Peters, Navy veteran Rocky Rochford, farmer Gavriel Soriano, state Representative Kevin Steele, builder Ergin Tek and former U.S. Attorney General Ashley Moody adviser Bea Valenti. Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball both list the race as Leans Republican. Castor serves as Ranking Member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Energy Subcommittee and previously chaired the Climate Crisis Select Committee.

hero.headline: Over 200 Martin County Kids Introduced to Tennis Through NJTL First Serve Program
hero.body:
The NJTL Boys & Girls Clubs of Martin County introduced more than 200 children to tennis through the First Serve experience program. The initiative brings tennis instruction to youth in Martin County through a partnership between the National Junior Tennis and Learning network and the local Boys & Girls Clubs.

The First Serve program provides children with their initial exposure to tennis, offering instruction and equipment to participants who might not otherwise have access to the sport. The program operates through the established infrastructure of the Boys & Girls Clubs facilities in Martin County.

The National Junior Tennis and Learning network has partnered with Boys & Girls Clubs chapters nationwide to expand youth access to tennis programs. The Martin County chapter joins other Florida NJTL chapters in delivering tennis instruction to underserved youth populations.

The program enrolled over 200 local children in its current session, marking a significant participation level for the Martin County chapter. The First Serve experience serves as an entry point for children to learn basic tennis skills and potentially continue with more advanced instruction through NJTL programming.

cards.headline: Woman Killed in Hobe Sound Mobile Home Fire
cards.teaser: Authorities have identified a woman who died in a mobile home fire in Hobe Sound.
cards.body:
A woman was killed in a mobile home fire in Hobe Sound, according to local authorities. Officials have released the identity of the victim following the deadly blaze.

The fire occurred at a mobile home in the Hobe Sound area of Martin County. Emergency responders were called to the scene where they discovered the victim.

Investigators are working to determine the cause of the fire. The incident remains under investigation by local fire and law enforcement officials.

cards.headline: Two Killed After Tesla Rear-Ended on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County
cards.teaser: A fatal crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County left two people dead after a Tesla was struck from behind.
cards.body:
Two people died following a crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County. The collision involved a Tesla that was hit from behind by another vehicle.

The fatal accident occurred on the turnpike as it passes through Martin County. Emergency responders arrived at the scene to find two victims who were pronounced dead.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances that led to the rear-end collision. The Florida Highway Patrol is handling the crash investigation.

cards.headline: Florida Board of Governors Confirms Dr. Stuart R. Bell as University of Florida President
cards.teaser: The Florida Board of Governors has confirmed Dr. Stuart R. Bell as the 14th president of the University of Florida.
cards.body:
Dr. Stuart R. Bell received final approval from the Florida Board of Governors to serve as the 14th president of the University of Florida. The confirmation completes the selection process for the state university system's flagship institution.

Bell comes to the University of Florida after serving as president at the University of Alabama. His tenure at Alabama spanned a decade during which the university experienced significant growth.

The Board of Governors vote makes Bell's appointment official. He will assume leadership of the University of Florida following the completion of the transition process.

cards.headline: Stuart Bell Named University of Florida President After Alabama Tenure
cards.teaser: Dr. Stuart Bell has been named the University of Florida's 14th president following a decade leading the University of Alabama.
cards.body:
The University of Florida Board of Governors confirmed Dr. Stuart Bell as the institution's 14th president. Bell spent the past decade as president of the University of Alabama, where the university experienced what officials described as a period of dominance.

The appointment brings Bell to lead one of the nation's largest public research universities. His selection followed a search process conducted by university officials and the state Board of Governors.

Bell's confirmation by the Board of Governors finalizes his appointment to the position. He will transition from his role at Alabama to assume the presidency at the University of Florida.

cards.headline: University of Florida Board Confirms Stuart Bell as New President
cards.teaser: Stuart Bell has won final approval to become the next president of the University of Florida.
cards.body:
Stuart Bell received confirmation from the Florida Board of Governors to serve as the University of Florida's president. The board's vote represents the final step in the approval process for the presidential appointment.

Bell previously served as president of the University of Alabama. He will now lead the University of Florida, one of the state's largest higher education institutions.

The confirmation allows Bell to begin the transition into his new role. University officials will work with Bell to facilitate the leadership change at the Gainesville campus.

cards.headline: Florida Board Approves Stuart Bell as UF's Next President
cards.teaser: The Florida Board of Governors has approved Stuart Bell to serve as the University of Florida's next president.
cards.body:
Stuart Bell won approval from the Florida Board of Governors to become the University of Florida's next president. The board vote officially confirms Bell's selection for the position.

Bell will transition from his current role to assume leadership of the University of Florida. The approval process included review by state education officials and the university system's governing board.

The University of Florida will now begin the transition process with Bell taking on presidential duties. He becomes the 14th person to serve as president of the institution.

hero.headline: Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties receive high grades in Florida school ratings
hero.teaser: The three Treasure Coast school districts scored high marks in newly released Florida school grades.
hero.body:
Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin counties all received high grades in the latest Florida school ratings released Wednesday. The grades reflect the performance of school districts across the state.

The Florida Department of Education released the grades as part of its annual accountability system. All three Treasure Coast counties scored above average in the state rankings.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce resident Norman E Godfrey dies
cards.teaser: Norman E Godfrey of Fort Pierce died. Services are being handled by Yates Funeral Home and Cremation Services in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Norman E Godfrey of Fort Pierce died Tuesday. Services are being handled by Yates Funeral Home and Cremation Services in Fort Pierce.

The funeral home announced the death on Tuesday, June 30, 2026. No additional service details were immediately available.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce and Port St. Lucie celebrate America's 250th birthday with fireworks and festivities Saturday
cards.teaser: America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone.
cards.body:
America turns 250 years old on Saturday, and communities across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast are pulling out all the stops to mark the milestone. From sunrise 5Ks and golf cart parades to drone shows, time capsule openings and spectacular fireworks displays, there is something for everyone this Independence Day.

Fort Pierce and Port St. Lucie are among numerous municipalities hosting celebrations. Delray Beach's annual Fourth of July Celebration begins at 8 a.m. and draws more than 20,000 people to East Atlantic Avenue and A1A. The day includes a 4's on the 4th Volleyball Tournament at the south end of the municipal beach from 8 a.m. to noon and a sand sculpting contest sponsored by Delray Beach Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs. At 5 p.m., the main festivities begin with the opening of a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule at the Main Stage at A1A, followed by a 60-foot flag raising with the National Anthem at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue at 6 p.m. Boca Raton's 68-year-old Independence Day tradition returns with events including the Firecracker 5K at 7:15 a.m. at Florida Atlantic University and the Liberty Cup Pickleball and Tennis Tournament at 8 a.m. A Fabulous Fourth Block Party runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Sugar Sand Park, with the Fabulous Finale at Countess de Hoernle Park from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m., featuring a 20-minute fireworks display at 9:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce drug bust uncovers 60.5 grams of meth and 43.5 grams of MDMA
cards.teaser: Authorities in Fort Pierce seized trafficking quantities of methamphetamine and MDMA in a drug bust.
cards.body:
Law enforcement officers in Fort Pierce discovered 60.5 grams of methamphetamine and 43.5 grams of MDMA in a trafficking bust. The quantities found meet the threshold for trafficking charges under Florida law.

The bust occurred Wednesday in Fort Pierce. Both methamphetamine and MDMA are controlled substances, and possession of the amounts seized typically carries enhanced penalties.

cards.headline: Kolter Homes adds new layout options for Port St. Lucie buyers
cards.teaser: Kolter Homes expanded home design personalization options for buyers in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Kolter Homes announced Tuesday it is expanding home design personalization with new layout options in Port St. Lucie. The homebuilder is offering additional floor plan configurations for buyers in the area.

The new layout options give Port St. Lucie homebuyers more choices when customizing their homes. Kolter Homes operates residential communities throughout Florida and offers various home designs to meet buyer preferences.

cards.headline: Oceanfront condo unit listed at 5051 N Highway A1A in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A residential unit at 5051 N Highway A1A Apartment 9-5 in Fort Pierce is listed for sale.
cards.body:
A condo unit at 5051 N Highway A1A Apartment 9-5 in Fort Pierce appeared on the real estate market Wednesday. The property is located on Highway A1A along the oceanfront corridor.

The listing represents one of the residential units available in the Fort Pierce area. Highway A1A runs along the Atlantic coast through St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach debuts drone show for 250th Independence Day celebration
cards.teaser: Lake Worth Beach will feature its first-ever drone light show Saturday as part of the city's Fourth of July celebration at Bryant Park.
cards.body:
Lake Worth Beach is celebrating America's 250th birthday with its first-ever drone show on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The event at Bryant Park will feature 300 drones performing for 15 minutes at 8:45 p.m., best viewed from Bryant Park facing southwest. The city is expecting to draw 10,000 people to the free event.

The day's schedule includes the Great American Raft Race at noon, hosted by the Neighborhood Association Presidents' Council, and a hot dog eating contest at 5:30 p.m. At 7:45 p.m., Vice Mayor Mimi May will participate in a skydiving performance with the All Veteran Group, carrying a special American flag commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary. Live music will be provided by Sekond Nature at 7 p.m. and Elton and the Jets at 8:30 and 9:30 p.m. A six-minute fireworks display with more than 11,700 shots launches at 9 p.m. The Lake Worth Beach Bridge will be closed to vehicles and pedestrians from 8 to 10 p.m. Ride-share drop-off is available at Fourth Avenue South and South Lakeside Drive at South Bryant Park.
